profile.campus: LightEdge Des Moines campus, Altoona, IA (DC1 and DC2, adjacent buildings on Northridge Circle)
profile.reading:
LightEdge Des Moines 1, also called DC1, sits at 1435 Northridge Circle in Altoona, Iowa, immediately next to LightEdge's other Des Moines-area building on the same street. Per LightEdge's own combined specification sheet for the two-building site, the pair together provide 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of total generator capacity with N+1 UPS redundancy, across 78,000 total square feet including 40,000 square feet of technical white space. LightEdge's sheet does not break those totals down between DC1 and DC2 individually, so no single-building capacity or square-footage figure is assigned to this specific record, and the same combined figures are recorded on the DC2 entry in this registry rather than duplicated as if each building carried the full campus total on its own.

The facility carries a broad, compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge's portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS, alongside NIST 800-53 and 800-171 alignment, with ten on-net carriers including Verizon, Lumen, Windstream, and Zayo.

LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa, though the company does not publish a formal street address for its headquarters on its own site. LightEdge announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm that also helped create Digital Realty in 2004, in September 2021. Then-CEO Jim Masterson said at the time that the deal would not change management, operations, or customer teams. Masterson led the company for 21 years before moving to an advisory board role at the end of 2024, and Rob Carter succeeded him as CEO on January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets, including Kansas City, Omaha, Ashburn, Phoenix, San Jose, and St. Louis alongside Des Moines, Austin, San Diego, and Minneapolis, plus one location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named publicly for this specific building.

Altoona sits just east of downtown Des Moines and has grown into a suburban technology and light-industrial corridor. The same suburb is also home to one of Meta's flagship data center campuses, which Facebook first opened in 2014 after choosing the area partly for access to wind-generated power from MidAmerican Energy, though Meta's much larger campus is a separate operation with no ownership or operational connection to LightEdge's smaller enterprise colocation site on Northridge Circle. LightEdge's decision to concentrate its own Iowa infrastructure in Altoona rather than in the Des Moines city core reflects the same land and power-availability considerations that shape data center site selection nationally.

reading.body:
LightEdge Des Moines 1 sits in Altoona, Iowa, immediately adjacent to a second LightEdge building on the same campus. The two-building site together provides 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of total generator capacity with N+1 UPS redundancy, across 78,000 square feet including 40,000 square feet of technical white space. LightEdge does not publish a per-building breakdown, so the individual contribution of DC1 cannot be separated from DC2's capacity. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a standard colocation density, the combined 6.1 MW of IT load translates to roughly 150 racks across both buildings.

The facility qualifies for SOC 1, 2, and 3 compliance, ISO 27001 and 20000-1 certification, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, PCI DSS compliance, and NIST 800-53 and 800-171 alignment. Ten on-net carriers including Verizon, Lumen, Windstream, and Zayo provide connectivity. No tenant is named publicly for this specific building.

In Iowa, this campus ranks third by published capacity among 52 mapped facilities statewide, accounting for roughly one-third of the state's two published megawatt figures totaling 18 MW. Iowa's small published capacity footprint reflects limited disclosure rather than limited infrastructure, as most mapped facilities publish no specifications. The Altoona location sits in the same suburb as Meta's much larger flagship data center campus, a separate operation chosen partly for access to wind-generated power from MidAmerican Energy, indicating the region's grid suitability for power-dense computing.
